data.title: Oil prices wrap up third straight weekly decline on strong Middle East supply outlook
data.description:
Crude oil futures edged higher on Friday but fell for the third consecutive week as recovering supply out of the Middle East outweighed concerns about ongoing strikes across the region, while President Trump continued to hold off on renewed large-scale attacks against Iran.

A stronger U.S. dollar and broader weakness across commodity markets also added to pressure on oil prices this week.

"Resilient flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain the story for energy markets broadly, extending to LNG recently," Macquarie energy strategist Walt Chancellor said in a note. "Should strength in Middle East flows and accompanying inventory builds persist, further oil price weakness would not surprise us."

Persistence of the status quo with the Iran blockade and convoys through the strait could keep pressure on oil markets, but "we cannot altogether dismiss the potential for escalation," Chancellor added.

In its World Energy Outlook, the Paris-based International Energy Agency said the global oil market is expected to return to a surplus as Middle Eastern production recovered faster than demand, forecasting an oversupply of 1.7M bbl/day in Q4 and widening to 3.8M bbl/day next year.

Data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration also pointed to improving regional supply, as Q3 oil shipments through major Middle Eastern chokepoints jumped 19% Q/Q while regional crude production reached 23.1M bbl/day in October, its highest level since the start of the Iran war, as producers expanded shipments through alternative routes.

However, Iran-backed Houthi militants said people near Saudi Arabia's Red Sea ports should evacuate and urged shipping companies to remove vessels, saying they would target Saudi ports in Jeddah and the Red Sea if a Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen's ‌Hodeidah port.

The warning came a day after the Houthis fired missiles at Riyadh, damaging several floors of a tower in the financial district.

Two oil tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said Thursday.

Iran's intensifying attacks on tankers transiting the strait, "running at roughly one incident per day in November," still add a meaningful geopolitical risk premium to the market, UOB Group analysts said in a note.

"Supply disruptions remain a risk, but near-term demand concerns tied to the AI trade unwind and broader risk-off sentiment are weighing on prices," Saxo Bank analysts wrote.

On Friday, front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for December delivery added 0.9% to $83.98/bbl, and front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for January delivery edged up 0.6% to $92.57/bbl; for the full week, Nymex and Brent fell 5.2% and 3.4%, respectively.

U.S. natural gas (NG1:COM) futures recovered from the previous day’s losses to settle at the highest level since February 6, with the front-month December contract climbing 4.4% to $3.411/MMBtu; for the week, natgas gained 5.6%.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), sank 6.8% this week.

data.title: Exxon greenlights $4B Angola oilfield development with new discovery, ANPG says
data.description:
Exxon Mobil (XOM) and its partners in ​Angola's offshore Block 15 have taken a ‌final investment decision on an estimated $4B redevelopment of the Kizomba A and B fields, while also announcing a hydrocarbon discovery ​in an exploration well, Angola's National Oil, ​Gas and Biofuels Agency said Friday.

The discovery ⁠at the Tchihumba West-01ST1 well was the 21st ​in Block 15 and the second this year and was ​made in one of Angola's most prolific deepwater oil-producing areas, according to ANPG.

The well was drilled to a water depth ​of nearly 4,600 ft and encountered 65.4 meters of sandstone ‌containing ⁠hydrocarbons with good petrophysical properties, ANPG said.

"Supported by the extension of the Block 15 production sharing agreement through 2037 and ~$4B in planned new investments, including the development of the Likembe field and activities under the Block 15 life extension project, we are well positioned to continue generating value for Angola, our partners, and our shareholders," Exxon (XOM) managing director Brian Unietis said.

data.title: Gold, silver end worst week in eight months but some analysts see signs of a bottom
data.description:
Gold's rout continued Friday ‌as the metal wrapped up its largest weekly loss in eight months, with the strong dollar, expectations of interest rate increases from the U.S. Federal Reserve, and the selloff in AI-linked stocks continuing to weigh broadly on commodities.

Stock markets fell around the world on Friday after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore faith in the AI trade, ​with investors cutting exposure and apparently taking profits ahead of the end of the year.

Gold's sharp slide has been exacerbated by comments from Fed policymakers that echoed hawkish tones in the FOMC's October meeting, with Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson the latest official to flag inflation risks that ​could warrant another rate hike.

Markets now see a 96% chance of a 25-bp U.S. rate hike in December, according to the CME's FedWatch tool.

Central bank buying should provide some support, but the pressure on precious metals could extend into next year until the market sees where the Fed ends up on interest rates, Everbank's president of world markets Chris Gaffney said.

"I'm not looking for that change anytime soon," possibly next year's Q1 or Q2, Gaffney said. "But once they say OK, I think we're good, I think that may be the start of the next leg up for gold."

Gold's failure to attract safe-haven demand during the equity market selloff suggests investors are selling liquid assets to cover losses and reduce risk, Saxo Bank's head of commodity strategy Ole Hansen said in a note.

However, holdings in gold ETFs have remained broadly unchanged over the past month despite the decline in prices, indicating longer-term investors have largely maintained their exposure, Hansen said, adding that gold's "best chance of a rebound may simply be that the selling has become excessive."

"Bond yields have eased somewhat, and the U.S. dollar has stabilized, [so] there is no obvious explanation for the continued and even accelerating decline in the gold price. Renewed forced selling may be playing a role following another selloff in technology stocks," Commerzbank analyst Carsten Fritsch said in a note.

The selling pressure on gold appears increasingly exaggerated, particularly as interest rate expectations have changed little in recent days, Fritsch added.

The U.S. dollar, which continues to trade near a 19-month high, remains a significant headwind for precious metals, Trade Nation senior market analyst David Morrison said, but any pullback in the dollar could provide gold and silver with some much-needed breathing room to stabilize.

On Friday, front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) for November delivery dipped 4.6% to $3,512.30/oz, its lowest settlement value since August 29, 2025, and front-month Comex November silver (XAGUSD:CUR) sank 7.4% to $41.035/oz, the lowest close since September 9, 2025.

For the full week, gold and silver sank 9.5% and 16.3%, respectively, with both metals recording their largest one-week declines since the week ending March 20.

data.title: Alps Group regains compliance with Nasdaq
data.description:
• Alps Group (ALPS) said on Friday it regained compliance with Nasdaq's $1 minimum bid price requirement after its shares closed at or above the threshold for 10 consecutive business days from Nov. 9 to Nov. 20.
  • Nasdaq confirmed that the compliance matter is closed.
  • The company had received a noncompliance notice in May 2026 after its shares traded below the $1 minimum bid price for 30 consecutive business days.
  • Share -3.36%

data.title: Abivax closes down 9% following short report
data.description:
Abivax (ABVX) closed Friday down ~9% following a short report from Scorpion Research, which attacked the clinical development of the company's ulcerative colitis candidate obefazimod.

Scorpion revealed it has a short position in Abivax. The firm claims that the asset exhibits "extreme" lipophilicity (dissolves more easily in fats, oils, and lipids rather than in water) on par with banned pesticides. As a result, this raises the risk of long-term tissue accumulation.

A drug that is more lipophilic than hydrophilic can more easily cross the blood-brain barrier, which is rich in lipids.

Scorpion questioned whether obefazimod "is even safe for livestock."

After the closing bell, Abivax responded, stating, "it is clear that the report contains numerous factually inaccurate and misleading statements, assumptions, and conclusions, including those based on studies commissioned and funded by Scorpion Capital itself. We firmly stand behind the integrity of our clinical development program, including the results of our Phase 3 ABTECT trials and the strength of the clinical data generated to date, which will support Abivax’s U.S. FDA NDA filing by the end of the year."

Due to Scorpion's short position, the company further alleged that Scorpion financially benefits from a decline in Abivax's share price.

data.title: Lockheed Martin wins $1.53B contract boost for Trident II missile work
data.description:
• Lockheed Martin (LMT) received an unpriced letter contract modification with a not-to-exceed value of $1.53B for TRIDENT II (D5) missile production and deployed systems support.
  • The work will be performed across multiple U.S. locations, with expected completion by September 30, 2031.  
  • The Strategic Systems Program is the contracting activity.

data.title: AI coding platform Cognition embarks on new $2B funding round: report
data.description:
Cognition AI, which offers an AI-powered coding and engineering platform, has entered talks for a new $2B funding round, which would elevate the startup to a $75B valuation, according to Bloomberg.

The company's primary products compete with Anthropic's (ANT) Claude Code, OpenAI's (OPENAI) Codex and SpaceX's (SPCX) Cursor, to name a few.

The San Francisco-based company has already raised more than $3B this year in other funding rounds, according to the report. Some of Cognition's clients include Wayfair (W), Cititgroup (C), and Mercedez-Benz (MBGAF). The company recently said it was on track to reach $1B in annualized revenue by the end of the year, which is double from four months ago.

data.title: Melar Acquisition changes name to Everli Global Holdings
data.description:

  • The Nasdaq Stock Market has approved the listing of Everli's Class A common stock and warrants on the Nasdaq Global Market, where they are expected to begin trading on November 23, 2026, under the ticker symbols "EVRL" and "EVRLW," respectively.
  • Press Release

data.title: Bayer’s $7.25B Roundup settlement approved by U.S. judge
data.description:
A Missouri judge on Friday approved Bayer's (BAYRY) (BAYZF) $7.25B settlement of lawsuits alleging its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer, which could help pave the way toward resolving litigation that ​has weighed on the company for a decade.

The agreement is "fair, reasonable, and adequate" and serves "the best interests of the class representatives," the Missouri Circuit Court judge said in his ruling approving the proposal.

Roundup litigation has posed a major headache for Bayer (BAYRY) (BAYZF), which inherited the legal troubles with its purchase of Monsanto in 2018; the shares tanked 80% in the years after the acquisition, although recent legal wins have helped recover some of the losses.

Bayer's (BAYRY) (BAYZF) settlement, announced in February, aims to resolve nearly all current and future Roundup ​claims in the U.S.

When Bayer (BAYRY) (BAYZF) unveiled the settlement, it was still awaiting a U.S. Supreme Court ruling on whether it could be sued over its government-approved warning label for Roundup; the company ultimately won the case, undercutting a ​central claim in many ​of the lawsuits against it.

The proposed settlement offers payouts ranging from $10K to $165K to ​people who were exposed to Roundup and developed non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with the ​exact award depending on the severity of their cancer, their age, and whether they were an occupational or residential user of Roundup.
